newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts English China Clays ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts English China Clays ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Monday it had lowered English China Clays Plc long-term ratings to BBB plus from A minus and short-term ratings to A2 from A1, and removed them from RatingWatch negative.
IBCA said in a statement English China Clays (ECC) was placed on RatingWatch with negative implications in September this year when the group revealed a sharp fall in interim profits.

"Unfavourable changes in both demand and supply of key products combined to cut H196 profits by 46 percent, or nearly 80 percent after exceptional restructuring charges. Operating profits for 1996 as a whole are not expected to show any improvement, partly due to further exceptional charges," IBCA said.

"The group's dependence on the paper industry, accounting for the majority of sales and profits, is now more pronounced than before the demerger of the construction materials business in 1994 and the withdrawal from housebuilding completed at the end of last year," the agency said. "Such divestments were aimed at reducing the seasonality and cyclicality of the group although it now appears that the sharp cyclical swings of the paper sector may have been underestimated."

IBCA said the reduced demand from paper manufacturers experienced in 1996 was partly explained by the slow and uncertain recovery of paper prices and associated downtime at several mills. Another factor was the structural fall in demand for kaolin in favour of ground calcium carbonate (GCC), which affected ECC's Brazilian sales in particular in H196.
"On the supply side, the already over-supplied kaolin market is beginning to see the effects of rapidly increasing exports from Brazil," IBCA said.
It said Speciality Chemicals, which was acquired in order to provide ECC with a high-margin, added-value business, was struggling due to continued cost-cutting by clients.

"A strategic review is under way," IBCA said. "The focus is on cost cutting in kaolin operations and the way forward is an increased emphasis on non-paper applications such as performance minerals and ceramics, where ECC also enjoy strong market shares."
"Despite increased financial and business pressures, the group's financial structure remains sound," the agency said.
